2561:Turn a document (a test plan, a QA checklist, a spreadsheet of scenarios) into runnable test cases with MCPJam's AI and add t
hem to the suite. Any text document works (markdown, JSON, CSV, plain notes), up to 100 KiB; the model reads the shape itself. **C
osts money:** each import consumes customer credits.
2577:| `--idempotency-key <key>` | No | Retry-safety key: repeating the call replays the first attempt's drafts instead of authori
ng (and billing) again |
2660:Send one message to a project's MCP servers and print the reply plus the raw tool calls, per-call latency and token usage: th
e telemetry a participant in the conversation cannot see.
2662:**This spends model credits on every call.**
2702:Print a session's per-turn execution spans: per-tool-call latency, token usage, and indices into the transcript.
166:| **Token budget under N** | Total token usage stayed below the cap. | Case only |
168:When an assertion is authored on an individual prompt turn it is evaluated against **that turn's slice** of the transcript: to
ol calls, assistant message, tool errors, and widget observations for that turn only. `Token budget under N` is case-only because
per-turn token usage is not reliably captured; all other assertions are turn-scopable.
176:> but for spend, two things replace it: [cost on every run](#cost), which shows
177:> what a suite actually costs, and `--max-cost-increase-percent`, which fails CI
179:> cap automatic credit purchases each month, see
253:> If **Run all** is disabled, no models are selected or a run for that suite is already in progress. For non-environment suite
s, a missing connected server also disables it. When every model the suite would run is out of MCPJam credits, **Run all** and eac
h case's **Run** button are disabled with an "Out of MCPJam credits · resets in …" tooltip, switching any case to a model from you
r own providers re-enables those buttons. The header pickers will tell you which condition applies.
448:* **Run insights**: an AI-written diff against your previous completed run: which cases moved, which tools changed behavior, w
hich models diverged. Skim this first; it usually points at the right rabbit hole. The model pass is **included with MCPJam and co
nsumes no credits**; it counts against a daily insight quota shared with swarm wave and user-testing insights. Guests browsing wit
hout a signed-in account will see a **Sign in** prompt in the insights band. Signing in unlocks the feature without losing your pl
ace.
486:When two or more host configurations are attached to a suite, a **By case / By host** toggle appears. **By host** shows a matr
ix: one column per host, one row per case. Each cell shows pass/fail dots, pass rate, median latency, and token usage. A host deta
ched after runs were recorded stays visible, labelled **historical**.
490:Every iteration carries the MCPJam-billed cost of the model work it did,
492:cost does not move later when prices change. It rolls up onto cases, runs and
495:A dash (`—`) means **no cost was observed**, never that the trial was free:
499:| Your own API key (BYOK) | MCPJam did not bill it, so there is no cost to report. |
500:| No token usage reported | Nothing to price. |
502:A cost your own SDK runner reported is shown but labelled **runner**: it is
508:alongside the cost and a cost gate treats partial coverage as non-gateable
532:* **Per-iteration row** with case, model, pass/fail, tokens, cost, duration, and the tool calls that actually happened. Each r
ow also shows a one-line summary of where that trial's user-value chain stopped (for example `broke at Tool response`, `Request sa
tisfied`, or `chain withheld`) so you can scan the table without opening each row.
546:Select any two completed runs and click **Compare**. The diff view shows per-case status changes: **Passed**, **Still failing*
*, **Regressed** (pass→fail), **Fixed** (fail→pass), **New**, **Removed**, and **Changed** (config differed). Summary metrics show
deltas for tokens, cost, and duration. In the per-run comparison table, metric deltas (pass rate, P50, P95, tokens) appear inline
beside their value rather than in separate Δ columns. Pass-rate movement is shown as a percentage delta (for example, `+10%`).
609:3. Delete the ones that don't match real usage; tighten assertions on the rest.
